They came under fire from infantry weapons which were left in the village during the escape. As they were shooting at the enemy, the groups also fired with anti-tank weapons, which resulted in the fires." Now, based on your testimony here, Mr. Krajina, that is a false report; isn't that right? It is -- it is inaccurate what -- the section that I just read to you is an inaccurate report?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no. Based on what I recall, I can state again that that's not how this event unfolded. And if you will allow me to, I should like to say something on this score. May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: It may have to do with this report. This report is written by the operation commander. It is a known matter that the operation commander would go to the starting line and wait for us. I never wrote a report in relation to the 26th of August, and I stand by what I said. I don't know where he obtained the information that these were the events that happened in the area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat what he just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajina, what are you doing is you are exploring what could explain that this was reported. However, Ms. Mahindaratne asked you one thing, is whether this report is accurate. And especially where the report says: "Both groups encountered resistance. They came under fire from infantry weapons, which were left in the village during the escape." That is not what you testified today. And to that extent, this report does not accurately reflect what you remember happened that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct, that it is not consistent with what I remember of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, at any stage, either when you got back to Zagreb on the 26th or sometime thereafter, was there a discussion amongst the four group leaders or members of the Lucko Unit as to what happened on the 26th August in the course of the operation? Did you discuss as to what happened, why you were sent to Zagreb, the smoke? Was there any discussion at all?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: There were no official discussions about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Unofficially?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No. Neither those, as far as I'm concerned. I don't remember talking to anyone on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krajina, your testimony is that, after -- at the -- when you -- I think -- let me just quote to you exactly what you said. This is at line -- page 26, line 15. You were asked as to what happened, you said: "Yes, we could see smoke as we were leaving the village, as we were at a certain distance from the village we could see smoke." Now, when you say "as we were leaving the village," this is the village of Ramljane, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So did you then inquire from anybody as to what the smoke was, what the cause of the smoke was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, later on, you discussed in your testimony that Mr. Markac arrived at the scene and that there was a discussion between Mr. Markac and Mr. Drljo. And you said that Mr. Markac probably spoke about the houses burning. Now, didn't you yourself want to find out as to how the houses burnt? You were a group leader; you led a group of men in the -- in the course of the operation. Didn't you think it would be appropriate for you to find out as to how the houses burnt?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I will say this first. I didn't say that General Markac came to the very place or that he came across our column on our way back. What I said was that he came across us toward the very end of the action. I didn't feel the need to have any additional discussions because I was responsible only for the group that was assigned to me. At the time, and I don't know how to put it, I believed that none of the members of my group did that, burn any houses. And I was not in a situation where I could put questions. What mattered to me was that my group had not done it. Since -- and also in view of the fact that by the time I had been instructor only for several days. I don't know if this answers your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did you find out later on as to which group was responsible for burning houses? And you said your group, you know -- knew was not responsible. But did you find out as to whether any other group was responsible for the burning of the houses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's an important thing missing in the translation. Page 56, line 8, after "I didn't say" -- that sentence, the second part of that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we read that then, again, to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The transcript tells us that you said: "I didn't say that General Markac came to the very place or that he came across our column on our way back. What I said was that he came across us toward the very end of the action." Now, Mr. Kuzmanovic says that this is not your complete answer. What did you say else from what I read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that General Markac came upon us or stopped us at a stretch of the road, and I couldn't tell you which exactly, after the end of the action, of the operation. If that had to do with your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This apparently satisfied Mr. Kuzmanovic. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, my previous question to you was: Did you, at any time afterwards, find out which group was responsible for burning the houses in Ramljane? You said your group wasn't. Did you find out which group was?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think the question lacks foundation, the first question. First it's compound, but -- if the witness could take his earphones off, Your Honour. I don't want do suggest the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take your earphones off, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The question should be, first of all, were -- was there a house or houses or anything burning in Ramljane, number one. And number two, if so, which group was responsible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that Ms. Mahindaratne put a very leading question because the question implied a fact which was not established, at least not by this witness. Therefore, it's leading, which --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe she can ask a leading question, Your Honour, but I think that question has a fact in it that needs to be established by this witness first before the second part can be asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although, that could also be considered part of the leading element, to include a fact. At the same time, it would not help us that much, Ms. Mahindaratne, if --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me break it into two, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, isn't is correct -- I'm sorry. Mr. Krajina, isn't it correct that in the course of the operation in Ramljane, members of the Lucko Unit - and I'm not directing this against you personally - but members of the Lucko Unit burnt house in the village of Ramljane?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did you find out, afterwards, as to who, which group, was responsible for the -- for that activity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, I didn't find it out nor was that in my line of duty to uncover these matters. This was not within my powers, nor did my role allow me to engage in uncovering who did what out in the field, especially when I know that the group had its leader and that it didn't have anything to do with me. Under those circumstances, I felt it best -- or, rather, I felt it -- I felt that the most important thing was that I knew for sure that it had not been done by anyone from my group.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, earlier on you said that Mr. Markac came to the -- and this is what you said: "I said that General Markac came upon us or stopped us at a stretch of the road, and I couldn't tell you which exactly, after the end of the action, of the operation." Now, isn't it correct that Mr. Markac, from -- and he was addressing you all and having a conversation with Mr. Drljo, from that position, one could see smoke and fire in the village of Ramljane? That is, the position where Mr. Markac was and the Lucko Unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you whether one could see smoke from that vantage point. I simply don't remember, and I wouldn't want to guess. Was this something that the lay -- that the lie of the land permitted, to see the smoke? And I don't want to guess whether he was able to see smoke from that point. But he somehow managed to see it or got to know about it which prompted him to stop our column. I don't know. Your question was whether, from that vantage point, when General Markac intercepted us, whether he was able to see smoke. I can't tell you that. I don't remember that. I don't remember the lie of the land. And I can't tell you if he was able to see it from that very spot or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I asked you that question because you have, in fact, discussed that issue when you were interviewed by the OTP in 2005. And let me just refresh your recollection on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Madam -- Mr. Registrar, if I could have 65 ter 7550, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And you were -- while that is it coming up, Mr. Krajina, let me tell you, you were questioned about the 26th August incident by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 439, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You -- this is what you said about -- what you could recall about the incident. You say: "He was angry. I can say that he was angry. He was unhappy about certain things, was unhappy about the fact that he could see smoke and fire." Now, does that refresh your recollection, Mr. Krajina? This is a statement you gave in 2005, four years back. At that time, you recall that Mr. Markac, from his vantage point, could see smoke and fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. Please interrupt me if this does not fall within my competence and my role here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you want to explain that the answer given does not necessarily contradict the other, then it would be beyond the scope. Because there's an issue to be unhappy to see something does not necessarily -- yes, if that's not the case, then please proceed, Ms. Tomanovic. Is it a comment which can be made with the witness listening?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it is. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Definitely. [Interpretation] I observed an interpretation error in the transcript. Since the witness gave his statement in Croatian and it was interpreted into English, this means that the controlling -- the version or the controlling version or the version which bears authority is the Croatian one. Perhaps you should ask the witness to read out what is written here as his statement in Croatian and then this might resolve the exchange that has been going on between him and the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I was going make the same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it appears a good suggestion to verify in this way what is in the original. Now, first of all, could we enlarge the relevant portion so that the witness can read it. Let me just see where ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... we should go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Up, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Further up. Yes, let me first -- one second, please, Ms. Mahindaratne. Yes, could you please read aloud what the -- the first answer you see on the screen, that is, the lines 1, 2, and 3. Could you please read that out aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading: "Well, he was angry. I mean, one has to say that. He was angry. He was unhappy about certain things. He was unhappy about the fact that mention was being made again of smoke and fire having been seen." Now, I can't say whether this is really ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have finished reading?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The end of the text, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've completed reading the first answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So the translation, Your Honour, is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's obvious, Mr. Kuzmanovic, having listened to -- to what was said. There's a clear difference. Ms. Mahindaratne, which makes perhaps your question moot.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, you are invited to move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Just one small question, Mr. Krajina. Here what you say is mention was being made again about smoke and fire. What did you mean, if you could recall, when you mentioned the word "mention was being made again about smoke and fire"? Were you referring to another incident where there was a mention of smoke and fire?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to give you the reason why I said it at the time. But there was no other incident, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I have only a couple -- couple of questions left for you. Now, after this incident on the 26th, there was, in fact, a discussion between the Chamber and yourself about going back to Zagreb. Now, isn't it correct that General Markac sent back the Lucko Unit to Zagreb immediately after this incident, without letting the unit participate in further operations, because he was angry. It was not because the activities had come to an end but because he was angry?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I will try to answer this question in the following way: I don't know in what way General Markac came to know or saw the smoke in the village of Ramljane.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I don't think you answered my question. My question was: Mr. Markac sent your unit back to Zagreb because he was angry with the unit; isn't that correct? Not because the unit had completed its tasks for which you were brought there, the unit was brought there, but because he was angry. He was withdrawing the unit from further activities and sending them -- sending you back to Zagreb. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, that isn't correct. And if you allow me, I will try and explain it to you and repeat what I said earlier on. We had completed --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you don't have to repeat. You know, what you said earlier is on record. But let me, in fact, point out to you what you said about this issue -- issue in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could you go to page 441 of this same document, 65 ter 7550.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There you can read what you said about this issue, Mr. Krajina. You say: "As far as I remember, the order came from his side, to stop that search operation and return to Zagreb." And you were asked the question: "And did he tell you why he was sending the Lucko Unit back to Zagreb?" Your answer is: "As I said, he wasn't happy about certain things, but he didn't give us a particular reason on the spot."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could go down to -- yes, and go to the next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And then you say: "... which we could consider as having completed the task and returning to Zagreb." Then you were asked the question: "But when you had, shall we say, completed your task on the second day, as you refer to it, were you expecting, when you set off, to go back to Gracac and to do another search the following day?" Your answer is: "It wasn't said, but I personally thought that we would continue, that we would have more search operations."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see the impeachment issue there, but I do have a question about line 14 of the previous page being incomplete -- incompletely translated. And -- or incorrectly translated. Mr. Krajina's answer in the statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move -- could we move to the previous page, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If the witness could just read that line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Line 14?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please read aloud what you are reported to have said, line 14. "Pa, dobro, mislim ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right. "I think, whether we, either ..." and then indistinct in brackets, "... did it to the end, I don't know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be quite far away from what has been translated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I mean, the word "Zagreb" doesn't appear, obviously, among other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, this seems that -- I don't know whether you want to further pursue that because there was this incomplete translation. There was another observation in the margin by Mr. Kuzmanovic, which you may not have missed. First, page 64, line 20, he started by a matter he did not further explain but which was, to some extent, clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. In view of the translation issue, I will move on. I will not pursue this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krajina, do you recall you made a statement -- at least -- I'm sorry, let me rephrase. Do you recall being interviewed by the Croatian authorities in 2001 on the incident in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I'll give you the answer in this way. I did make a certain statement in the Ministry of Interior, that is to say, the police administration, the Zagreb one, linked to those events. I can't tell you the exact date. I don't remember the exact date. Perhaps it's the date that you mentioned. Most probably it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me show you the note of interview, Mr. Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have P1087, please. P1087.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Tomanovic, take care next time that the microphones are switched off if you consult with Mr. Krajina. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And while that document is coming up, Mr. Krajina, I want to tell you I'm just moving to a couple of questions on Grubori, so you might want to pay attention to what's being asked? Could you just go through this note, Mr. Krajina, and tell the Trial Chamber whether this note accurately reflects what you stated to the police in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if, Mr. President, in the interests of time, if my colleague's instructions are based on the instructions if the witness is not going to answer, we don't have to waste time for him to read this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do not expect Ms. Tomanovic to give instructions but, rather, advise. But if the witness would, on the basis of the advice or for any other reason, would object to answer this question because the answer would tend to incriminate himself, then we'd like to know right away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we don't have to waste time on this document. Mr. Krajina, just one -- one more question. In the course of the operation on 25th August, is it correct that none of the groups, none of the four groups, met with resistance from enemy groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina objects to answering the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just want to place on record, in view of Mr. Krajina clearly exercising his right against self-incrimination with regard to this subject, I will not explore any other matters with regard to the events in Grubori.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question arises what you could conclude from that. Apparently you are suggesting that has anything to be concluded rather than to establish that he used his right. But let's move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I just want to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have 65 ter 7666.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I asked you previously about your promotion. There is no dispute about it. I just want you to take a look at this document and confirm if it is based on this document that you were promoted in 1996. I believe you said you were promoted as assistant commander in 1996.

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: But that wasn't the official decision appointing me to the post of assistant commander. It doesn't look like an official document, like that official document, the official decision appointing me to the post of assistant commander of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I didn't say official decision. I asked you whether, based on this proposal, you were promoted, whether based on this proposal. This may not be the official decision; it is a proposal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: The proposal is probably correct. But I wasn't even informed about how the proposal -- what the proposal looked like, nor did I know who proposed me. I was informed in -- or, rather, my colleague and I were informed, and he was also proposed to become assistant commander, we were called to General Markac's office, and we were essentially told then. Now, when the decision came in, what date was on it, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll stipulate that this is the proposal from General Markac that Mr. Krajina be promoted. The question related to whether this document confirmed his promotion, it's clear the document does not. It happened later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It's in -- yes. Let's move on. It's clear that this is a request rather than a decision. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I tender this document into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2728. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2728 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, based on -- just I -- I just wanted to conclude. But if I could have just a minute to ask the witness just two more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have one minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I just want to -- I did tell you that I will not ask you about any questions with regard to Grubori, but let me just ask you two questions. Is it correct that members of the Lucko Unit - and I'm not directing [Realtime transcript read in error "I'm directing"] this allegation against you in -- personally - is it correct that members of the Lucko Unit killed the civilians in Grubori on 25th August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correction to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for Ms. Tomanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes, just a correction to the transcript. On page 69, line 17, I think the Prosecutor said I'm "not" directing this allegation against you. And the transcript says otherwise. So I think it should be corrected. The interpretation was okay, but the transcript as recorded in English was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think you said that you were not directing this allegation against the witness and that is how it was translated. And I think it's the first mistake in the last couple of weeks that I noticed from our transcriber. I wish we all would make such a low number of mistakes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My second question to you, Mr. Krajina, is: Isn't it correct that members of the Lucko Unit burnt houses in Grubori on 25th August?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I have no further questions to you, Mr. Krajina. Thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Mahindaratne. Mr. Kuzmanovic, are you ready to start your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Let me just get set up here, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajina, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Kuzmanovic is counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Krajina.

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I just wanted to follow up on an issue that the Prosecutor asked you about, relating to your proposal for promotion. Procedurally that proposal would go to your commander, which is Mr. Turkalj, correct, at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No. No, that wasn't the rule. Because the proposal could have been written by the commander too. And it all went to the special police sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then who would eventually be the person, then, to approve your promotion?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, in all this, well, I couldn't tell you who approved it. But who gave agreement to those promotions, who agreed to them, was Mr. Markac, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I want to ask you questions about the 26th of August, 1995. And, in particular, we're going to be referring at times to your statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor on January 11th, 2005, which is 65 ter 7550.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So if Mr. Registrar could just have that handy, we may be referring to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 86 of that document, the -- 86 is not the e-court number, it's the -- page 86 of 108. That's how I have the document in my binder, which is the last portion of the interview. And for assistance, it would be V000-5273.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's the correct page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Before you look at that, Mr. Krajina, I wanted to ask you, in this interview, you were asked, when you were spoken to by General Markac, who else was in his group. And your recollection at that time was Mr. Janic was there. You were also asked about Mr. Sacic, and you said you didn't recall seeing Mr. Sacic there at that particular time on the 26th. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: And I say the same now. I don't remember Mr. Sacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You have -- you are familiar with Mr. Sacic, are you not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: He is someone that can't be missed, in terms of being able to hear him and see him. He's got a rather loud way of expressing himself, does he not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were Mr. Balunovic and Mr. Zinic present on the 26th, as far as you can recall, when General Markac met you with the column?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I've already said, of all those that you mentioned, the whole unit was there, because we were on our return.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that the operation on the 26th had anything to do with the freedom train?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Yes, it was linked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you aware that the Lucko Unit was assigned to this portion of the tracks in which the freedom train would travel because it was considered to be one of the more sensitive areas of the entire trip?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: We were given our assignment, so probably the assumption was that that was a sensitive part of the track. And since our assignment was to search and to see in a certain way that the train could pass by unimpeded and reach Split, then we provided security for that section.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that something that was done along the tracks, or was that also done in-depth, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: It was probably -- probably a certain belt was taken along the tracks, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you were asked questions about what happened during that particular search operation and security operation for the freedom train on the 26th. Did you personally observe anybody burning any buildings at all on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I'll try and answer this and tell you how we viewed it and experienced it. Passing through the village, well, may I take a little time to explain? Because I don't want to be in a situation whereby I have to just say yes or no. I would like to paint the picture to you, what the situation was like, and why I'm saying that. At the exit of the village, all we had once we had passed the village -- it was only then that you could see the smoke. And practice has shown that most often, when you want -- or when someone wants to set fire to a house, for instance, then all they have to do is to rush into the house for a split second and set fire to a curtain, for example, with a lighter. And you can move quite far away without ever noticing that somebody was -- that something was burning in the house. So it takes a long time for the actual smoke to appear. Therefore, it's difficult, given that kind of situation, to say, Yes, I saw somebody set fire. As I say, it only takes a split second to go inside, to set something alight, and then you can be away quite a distance, quite a long way away from the place where this was happening, and then you see nothing anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I appreciate your answer, but my question was pretty simple. Did you personally observe anybody burning any buildings at all on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can a house or any building be set afire either through weapons fire from a gun or a hand-held rocket-launcher or anything of that nature? In your experience.

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: As far as I know, it all depends on the ammunition and the explosive devices, the anti-armour devices, and hitting a certain object. If a certain object is hit, it doesn't necessarily lead to flames and burning. As far as ammunition is concerned, then you have certain ammunitions which, for example, if you fire a number of bullets, yes, the object targeted can be set aflame. But with the ammunition that you -- we used, that is quite simply impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic [sic], during your search you were asked on page 58 of 108 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My error.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I apologise for that. You were asked, on page 58 of 108 of your statement to the OTP, you were asked: "During that search, do you recall an incident taking place" -- meaning on the 26th, and you answered "No." And then the next question was: "This is where -- this -- this is where there was a lot of gun-fire and a village was set on fire?" And then you asked: "The second day?" And the answer from the person who was questioning you: "Yes," that being the 26th. Do you recall anyone in the Lucko Unit on the 26th talking about a village being set on fire, or was that something that the investigator assumed had taken place when he asked you that question?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, I can't say that anyone was talking on that day about some events like that. It was probably a conclusion made by -- well, I don't know. I really don't know how to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, at any time, Mr. Krajina, observe that a village was set on fire in the Ramljane operation on the 26th of August, 1995, by members of the Lucko Unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Linked to the previous answers, let's try and answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it is a pretty simple question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think the witness should be allowed to answer, Mr. President. This is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This is cross-examination, and the Judge is the one who will -- who decides on who can ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic, and if the witness, in phrasing his question [sic], says, I'd like to look at the previous questions, then he's allowed to do so. Could you please continue, Mr. Krajina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say was - and I will be brief - I've already said before that it was visible, that we could see upon exiting the village, and I'm mentioning this for the 26th, that you can see -- well, it was obvious and visible that there was smoke. So obviously the village did not set fire to itself. Some member of the unit certainly set fire to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As for how that happened and when that happened, you can't give us any details; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know any of the details. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, in that part of the search operation on the 26th of August, 1995, you did observe, did you not, houses that had been destroyed in the years prior, before the Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear on what you're asking me. Could you repeat the question? Are you thinking about the period --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see, when you were going through on your search operation on August 26th, 1995, any buildings that had been destroyed prior to Operation Storm by the people who had occupied that area of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: If I can say, well, you -- you call it buildings. We would call it differently. They certainly weren't buildings. They were hamlets, and the houses were built with some sort of ... some sort of stones. And they were already in a state of disrepair. I can't say that I actually saw that they had been destroyed in any way or -- but that they were in ruin or in disrepair, that's something that I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I'd like to take you to page 60 of your transcript with the OTP, which was in January of 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that page 50 in e-court, or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I have them numbered by pages of transcript. It's -- it's the same section of transcript that we just had in front of us. Page 60 of 108. Yes, that's the page on the screen. Thank you. If we could scroll down, please. That's good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, I'd like to read you the section starting at line 27 and go to the next page. So I will start with line 27, and the question is -- and I will ask a question after I read this section: "And do you remember any conversation over the radio in which, I think, Mr. Celic asked what was going on, why there had been smoke coming from a village?" And your answer is: "I don't remember that."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we go to the next page. That's not the next page. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you say: "I don't remember that." And then the question is: "You don't remember that? And you say: "I don't remember that." But it's translated as: "Okay." Line 16: "And [sic] as a result of this, and the fact that the freedom train was due to run very shortly, you know, within a few days of this search, Mr. Markac was in the area, were you aware of that?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, where you said it was translated as "Okay," that's not the case. The answer is not translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the person who interviewed Mr. Krajina said "Okay." Now, the answer was rather short. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think we can all stipulate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most likely -- most likely the gist of answer was clear already to the [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, Your Honour, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'll continue on -- thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On line 16, the question is: "As a result of this, and the fact that the freedom train was due to run very shortly, you know, within a few days of this search, Mr. Markac was in the area, were you aware of that?" And the answer is: "That was on the second day." As far as I remember. Now, Mr. Krajina, I'm just going to submit to you that this passage that I read relates -- and the conversation over the radio with Mr. Celic relates to August 25th and not August 26th and that you are mixing the two up. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, what is the basis for this suggestion because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kuzmanovic is asking a question. Now, I must admit that it's not entirely clear to me what Mr. Kuzmanovic asks may have been mixed up. At the same time, I'm looking at the clock. And I missed already --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. So did I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the time at which we should stop. Therefore, perhaps you think about rephrasing your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so that it at least meets my concern and possibly, as well, Ms. Mahindaratne's concern. We'll have a break for one hour. That means that we will resume at five minutes to 3.00. Mr. Kuzmanovic, is the estimate of the time you will need still the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I will be done well within that -- well within the next 20 minutes after that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next 20 minutes after that. And then the parties are invited to remain stand by - and not for you, Ms. Tomanovic - to deal with some housekeeping matters after that. We'll resume at five minutes to 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.52 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, the previous question that I asked you before the break, I'm going withdraw. I'll ask you a different question. On -- the Presiding Judge had asked on page 26 of today's transcript, line 15, referring to the operation on the 26th of August: "Did you see any smoke or any fire on that day?" And your answer was: "Yes. We -- we could see smoke as we were leaving the village, as we were at a certain distance from the village, we could see smoke." Now, that -- how far -- how far was the distance that you were at from the village where you saw the smoke?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I want to take you to your statement related to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 58, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: -- that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's 432 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Before I get there, Mr. Krajina, you know the difference between a village and a particular building or a house or barn, do you not? And there is a difference. A village is a collection of buildings and a house or a barn -- or a building is one individual unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You were asked by the investigator for the Prosecution's Office on line 5: "During that search" -- again, referring to the 26th of August, "do you recall an incident taking place?" And you answered: "No." On line 13, the investigator asked you: "This is where there was lot of gun-fire and a village was set on fire?" And then you asked: "The second day?" And then you continued on with your answer. Mr. Krajina, as you sit here today, would you agree with me that there was not an entire village set on fire on August 26th, 1995, that this was something that was stated to you by the Office of the Prosecutor's investigator and not by you?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President. I object, Mr. President. I don't think the -- the counsel Mr. Kuzmanovic is referring to a statement made by this witness at a previous stage in the course of the interview, and I don't know whether Mr. Kuzmanovic is trying to impeach the witness with this statement or refresh his recollection, but this statement which is before us is not in evidence. So I'm not clear as to what is going on. The suggestion that the OTP has made a statement to the effect that a village has been set on fire is not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at the same time, I think it was read to the witness, at least it was now read to the witness, and for very practical reasons I think that the Chamber gave guidance to the parties that if there was anything which would be inconsistent, but that would, of course, also cover if something is unclear, that by reading the relevant portion of the statement we would avoid that we'd have a discussion as to whether the whole of the statement would be in evidence or not. So, therefore, the objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, do you -- can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, I can't assert that a whole village was burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing you can confirm is that you saw smoke?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Yes. From a certain distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could please go to page 63 of the same OTP witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if we could go to line 15 of that, please. Line 18, I mean, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This was -- I'm referring you now to the issue that the Presiding Judge discussed with you on the -- on Mr. Drljo. And you told the Presiding Judge on today's transcript - I don't have the exact page reference, but I have the transcript in front of me. I think it's page 30 ... 31 and 32. Where the Judge asked you: "You said based on what you heard. You mean personally observed, you heard when that argument was going on?" And you answered: "Yes. While I was there, I was listening to that part of their conversation." And the question was: "Yes. What did Mr. Drljo say?" And you said: "Well, I don't know how precise I can be in trying to quote their words. I think it was roughly the following: What was it that I did? "Well, I can't really repeat the words because I don't remember them. But I think the gist of what ... he said is something I conveyed." And then the Judge asked you: "What was it that Mr. Drljo said in response to Mr. Markac?" And you answered: "Well, I guess the gist was I did it so what can you do about it? What can you do to me?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's just, for reference, to page 33 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you were very specific, when answering Judge Orie's questions, about the confrontation between Mr. Drljo and General Markac on the way back from the operation in Ramljane on August 26th. However, when you talked to the Prosecutor's Office five years ago in 2005, you were asked: "Do you remember" -- on line 18 "him" -- meaning Mr. Markac "having sort of a very close face-to-face with Mr. Drljo, you know, heated words between them?" And the answer was -- actually, [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you said: "As far as I remember, he did not address anybody in particular." And then on the next page, on line 8: "As far as I remember, he waited for us at a certain point, the convoy stopped, and we all -- I think it was all of us, we came out of our vehicles and that's when he addressed us in a certain way." Now, Mr. Krajina, back in 2005 you mentioned nothing about the issue of a direct confrontation that Mr. Markac had with Mr. Drljo; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There is further reference on that conversation at page 436 onwards where the witness has discussed conversations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please look at it and see whether the factual basis for your question still stands, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. If you could give me the page of 108, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... in the fourth section, page 62. And on e-court it's 436.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the section where it says: "Do you remember, when you were leaving the convoy, the Lucko Unit, the convoy being stopped and Mr. Markac approaching members of the Lucko Unit?" And he says, on the next page: "He was at a certain position, and he waited for us as we were coming back." And the next line is: "And do you remember him speaking to members of the Lucko Unit?" And the answer is: "Yes, I think that's what happened, as far as I remember." And then, further on, he says he doesn't remember anything about Drljo. So I don't see where this adds to the clarity. There's nothing in this statement that says that he had a face-to-face confrontation with Mr. Drljo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Reference to Mr. Drljo, but if you see, from line 30 onwards of page -- of the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you mean where he says: "As far as I remember, he did not address anybody in particular." That part?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Page 64, line 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: "I can say in a certain way and I remember the words, but I can't" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have that on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That would be on e-court page 436 onwards, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I still don't see anything in here about any confrontation between Mr. Drljo and Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to point out there was more evidence about the conversation, not only the portion that you read, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the issue is whether it was a specific conversation between two persons or whether it was -- whether it was addressing the unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think when I asked questions about it, I asked whether any of the members responded. And then I think it was when Mr. Drljo came up. Now, whether you consider that a one-to-one conversation in the presence of others or addressing a group, one of the members of the group responding, that's, of course, is -- well, that's to some extent a matter of perception and definition as well. But please proceed, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, back in 2005, you made no mention at all of any direct exchange between Mr. Markac and Mr. Drljo. That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to say exactly what I said back in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... showing you your statement here that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Krajina, and no where in this statement did you specifically address a conversation that Mr. Markac had with Mr. Drljo and the fact that Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, in order for the witness to truthfully answer that question, of course, he would have to read the whole of the statement. The parties and the Chamber is able to see whether it was mentioned or not. Just put it to him and whether he verifies or not. Apparently you want to say you didn't -- you described the situation not as a direct one-to-one conversation between Mr. Markac addressing Mr. Drljo and Mr. Drljo answering to that.

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, Mr. Krajina, Mr. Kuzmanovic has not found anything in that statement where you describe the situation as Mr. Markac addressing Mr. Drljo, Mr. Drljo answering to Mr. Markac, whereas it seems that from what was just read is that Mr. Markac addressed the group or group leaders or at least a number of people where Mr. Drljo apparently responded to what Mr. Markac had said, even if not directly to him. That's what Mr. Kuzmanovic, I take it, will ask you a question about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You did not address that issue between -- as -- you did not describe that issue as a direct confrontation between Mr. Markac and Mr. Drljo, correct, back in 2005?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, I can't really assert from the position that I had at the time where I was at the time, whether he directly addressed Drljo or not. I don't know if I've made myself clear. But certain discussions did take place between the two of them. That I can say. Perhaps the address was intended for the unit as a whole. I can't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... telling us now here, Mr. Krajina, as you sit here today you don't know whether General Markac was specifically addressing Mr. Drljo and not the whole unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, there was ongoing discussion at the time I joined the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What that discussion was, who was addressing whom, you can't tell us; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, let me answer this way: That's correct. I cannot state now that it was Mr. Drljo who was addressed. Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, have you had a chance to review all of the documents and statements that were given to the Croatian authorities involving the matter that is going on in Croatia, in which you are an accused?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I haven't had a -- that chance. I did not read the documents. I did not talk to anyone. I have, for the past four months, been in the remand facility, and the only documents that I looked at were the ones that my lawyer was able to send me. So I have been unable and I am still unable to gain an insight into these documents, to read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, maybe my question wasn't clear. I'm not referring to any documents here at the ICTY or any pieces of evidence here or anything like that. What I'm referring to is statements that were made before investigative judges, in Croatia, relating to the case in which you are an accused. Did you have a chance to review any of those documents from other witnesses or accused before coming here?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, His Honour showed -- no, it wasn't His Honour. I believe it was Ms. Mahindaratne showed P767 to you. I'd like -- which was a report written by Mr. Celic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What I'd like to ask the Registrar, please, to put up P768.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, were you aware that Mr. Drljo, Mr. Zinic, and Mr. Balunovic all wrote reports relating to August 26th, 1995, to the action?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you asked by Mr. Celic or Mr. Janic to write a report about what occurred on August 26th?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you near a group which was being led by either Mr. Drljo, Mr. Zinic, or Mr. Balunovic on August 26th?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Close to the group led by Mr. Zinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could please pull up P769.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report dated August 26th, 1995, signed --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll down a little bit to see what appears to be at least -- perhaps not a signature, but Mr. Zinic's name is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And there's been evidence in the case that stated Mr. Zinic recognised that and the handwriting as being his. Were you within close enough distance to Mr. Zinic to observe whether or not there was fire from his unit, meaning weapons fire, from the group that he was leading?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I was close enough to Mr. Zinic because we were advancing along a road. But I can't tell you what it was that his members of the group did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So if, in his report, Mr. Zinic stated, among other things, that he had noticed some buildings had been set on fire and some were still smouldering and that when he arrived -- "we arrived in the hamlet of Vucenovici, we came under fire from some houses, and we returned fire." Would you be able to tell me whether you were in a position to say anything contrary to what Mr. Zinic has reported in P769?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: In answer to your question, I can only tell you that no buildings were on fire and we didn't come under any fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe my question was too long and convoluted. My question to you, Mr. Krajina, is that: Are you in a position to say anything about Mr. Zinic's report that is counter to what he wrote in his report about what he experienced?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe the question was asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was asked but not answered. Please proceed, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Not to say that an answer was given, but it was not a direct answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, can you please answer that question for us. If you want me, I can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Can you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. Are you in a position, Mr. Krajina, to say anything about Mr. Zinic's report of the 26th of August that is counter to what he wrote in his report about what he experienced or his unit experienced?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I can tell you only one thing and that that's -- well, first of all, I have not read his report, even now, and I'm not familiar with it, and I can only tell you that this is not how things happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I guess my question to you, Mr. Zinic [sic], is let's assume for a moment that what Mr. Zinic reported in his report is accurate. What I want you to answer for us, please, is were you in a position to say something or to observe something contrary to what Mr. Zinic's unit observed?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object to that question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic. If the witness says, This is not how it happened. Then to say, Could you have observed it if it would be true, that's more or less ignoring the previous answer of the witness. And if you would carefully look at the transcript of today, you find a few places where already one might find an answer to your question. I'm not further elaborating on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, did you ever have an opportunity to speak with anyone from the Lucko Unit about what occurred on August 26th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Let me answer this way: I can't say that I did not have occasion to, since we were in the same unit, that we didn't have occasion to speak, but we did not talk about it. And my explanation for it is that as time progressed in the subsequent period, I did not spend that much time in the unit and with members of the unit since I was assigned to assignments of quite a different nature, and my presence in the unit was only sporadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note that I may have misspoke on line 18 of page 90 and called the witness, again, Mr. Zinic or a name that he isn't. But it's noted as "Zinic" there; it should be "Krajina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajina, can you please tell us whether at any time you, other than observing General Markac on the road back after the operation on the 26th, had any conversation of any kind with General Markac relating to this issue?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions from the Cermak Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same for the Gotovina Defence. Could I ask you to take off your earphones for a second. I'm addressing the parties for a minute. I invited the witness who said he didn't know whether they moved east to west or west to east whether a map would assist him. I think he said south-east to north-west in the beginning then when looking at the map he said we went in easterly direction. Now, all the other evidence suggests the opposite direction that is from east to west. When I say the other evidence, I'm mainly referring to the reports of the three group leaders and the report by Mr. Celic. And it's described there in some detail about the starting Kaldrma and one group going Dobrici Vujekovici and then, I think, ending up in Perica tor. And the other group, let's say the Zinic/Krajina group, described as operating on the axis Cosici and then Vucenovici then Topica - I have to check that - but that appears on the map as somewhere on the slopes of Mount Promina. So all the other evidence goes in the different direction. Now, I could take the witness back to that, but if all parties would agree that the movement was in the opposite direction compared to what the witness said, then I don't have to pay further attention to it, although I may have one or two questions which I relate to that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in agreement with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not hear from the other Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: We're in agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put your earphones on again. Further Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Mr. Krajina, at what time approximately was the operation concluded on the 26th of August?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours. I couldn't give you the exact hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it -- do you remember whether it was late afternoon or early afternoon?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Let's say in the earlier part of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that mean around 3.00 or 2.00 or 4.00?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I would say roughly around 2.00 or 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you several times referred to "the village." You also talked about the village of Ramljane. You described that the groups got together, reunited again in the village. Was that the four groups or the -- at least all the men of the four group leaders?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I was saying that I had met Mr. Zinic. I didn't mention the other groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, was that in the beginning or at -- almost at the end of the operation? The earlier stages or the late stages?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: That encounter could have happened before we entered the village or in the village itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are talking about "the village," are you talking about the village which you visited in the earlier stages or -- where you passed through in the earlier stages of the operation or in the late stages? Was it close to the end or close to the beginning of the operation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Closer to the very beginning of the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you described the operation as going from west to east, after had you consulted the map. I just inquired with the -- no, let's me say the following: That would put Ramljane village almost at the end of the operation. I asked the parties in this case, on the basis of other evidence we received, whether they had concluded on the basis of the other evidence that it was likely that the units would have moved from east to west. Do you consider it a possibility that you made a mistake even after having consulted the map, that you moved from west to east; whereas, the other evidence suggests that it was from east to west?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, actually, I may have made a mistake. Looking at the map, I routinely said west/east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you say it might be -- might have been the other way. I don't know why you routinely say west/east. But you consider that this may be a mistake, and it could have been east/west; or are you even certain that, on the basis of the map, that it would have been east/west.

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, I cannot be certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you're unable to say with some certainty whether it was in the direction, as you testified this morning, or whether it was in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I am convinced now that we were moving from the east in a westerly direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you told us that when you left the village you saw smoke. Now, was that in the very early stages of the operation; or was it the middle of the operation; was it at the end of the operation? Could you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I cannot say in which stage of the operation that was. But I did point out that it was once we had left the village or were about to leave it. I cannot say with certainty when we got to the village. In which stage of the operation, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, other evidence suggests that you did not pass through just one village but through more villages or hamlets or at least groups of houses. Do you have any comment on that? Do you consider this a possibility? Because you're always talking about "the village."

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: I remember just that village. And later on, I did mention that we came across some houses. And I mentioned again reaching some building and some people, but I can't remember how many villages we passed through or how many houses we saw. And that's really -- and that really isn't anything I can say with certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I earlier asked you about whether you meant, with "the village," "Ramljane." Now, when you told us about the smoke you saw after you had left the village, are you sure that it was a village which was called Ramljane?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: Well, only that village, with that name, remains in my memory. I don't remember other villages. I wouldn't remember them either by name or for any other reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Other evidence suggests that events have -- may -- taken place either in a village called Vujakovici, which is in the Ramljane area, and Vucenovici, which is also -- at least if I look at P190, is still in an area which is called Ramljane. Is that something you consider to be possible, that it is a hamlet or a small village in an area called Ramljane, where the village or hamlet itself had one of the names I just mentioned to you, that is, Vujakovici or Vucenovici?

utterances.speaker: BOZO KRAJINA
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to tell now. I already said that I don't remember the names of those villages. It's difficult for me to tell whether it happened there, after all. But I repeat that only Ramljane is still in my memory, is something I remember. And I can only speak about events that I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no further questions for you. Have the questions of the Bench triggered any need for further examination? Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: None of the other parties? Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Krajina, this concludes your testimony in this Court. I thank you for coming to The Hague. I thank you for having answered many of the questions that were put to you by the Bench and by the parties, and I hope that you have a safe return to your country. Ms. Tomanovic, I'd like to thank you for being available on such a short notice to assist the witness. We'll continue with the case, but you -- your presence is not needed. Of course, you can follow the proceedings if you wish to do so, but it's -- may be -- housekeeping may be rather boring for an outsider. Then, Mr. Krajina, I'll ask you to be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just wish to say that it was my pleasure to assist the Trial Chamber. I'm glad that you have entrusted me this role. Certainly there is no need for me to stay in the courtroom, so I ask for permission to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Permission is granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to briefly deal with a few procedural matters. It may not take very long. The first is the following: On the -- and this is more or less to inform the public about an event. On the 21st of April, 2010, the Chamber granted a motion of the Prosecution to re-open its case. The decision was filed confidentially. A public version will be made available in due course. The Chamber also suspended the dead-line for filing final briefs, which was originally mentioned at transcript page 28047. The second item is that -- that the Chamber now issues a decision with regard to the relief requested in - I quote: "Gotovina Defence submission in response to Trial Chamber invitation of 29th of March, 2010." On the 26th of March, the Chamber made a statement regarding the content of the final briefs of the parties. This statement can be found at transcript page 28.048. On the 29th of March, 2010, following several informal communications from the Gotovina Defence and the Prosecution, the Chamber granted the Gotovina Defence leave to file a submission on this matter, and informed the parties accordingly through an informal communication. On the 7th of April, the Gotovina Defence filed its submission, requesting that the Chamber clarify its statement by instructing the Prosecution not to include certain new specified allegations in its final brief. On the 8th of April, 2010, the Markac Defence joined that submission. And on the 19th of April, the Prosecution filed a response, requesting that the Chamber deny the relief requested by the Defence. The Gotovina Defence submitted that the Chamber's invitation, and I quote: "Calls upon the Prosecution to particularise allegations against General Gotovina that have never been specified previously." The Chamber's statement merely identified certain categories of evidence that it would find helpful if the parties were to refer to in their final briefs. It was addressed to the Prosecution in particular because the Prosecution bears the burden of proof. The Chamber did not invite the Prosecution to further specify its allegations, and the specificity of the pleadings has already been litigated and decided upon. Therefore, the Chamber denies the Defence request. And this concludes the Chamber's decision on the Defence request regarding the Chamber's statement of the 26th of March, 2010. The Chamber would now like to issue its decision on the Gotovina Defence's motion requesting the Chamber to decide on certain motions no later than 30th of April, 2010. The Gotovina Defence filed this motion on the 1st of April, 2010. The two motions that the Gotovina Defence requests the Chamber to decide on by the said date are the Prosecution's Rule 54 bis motion, with regard to Croatia, and the Gotovina Defence's Rule 54 bis motion, with regard to the European Union Monitoring Mission. The Prosecution responded on the 15th of April, 2010, stating that the Gotovina Defence has failed to show that the Chamber has unreasonably delayed its issuance of decisions on these two motions. On the 16th of April, 2010, Croatia filed a letter, stressing the urgency of the Prosecution's Rule 54 bis motion. On the 19th of April, the Gotovina Defence requested leave to reply. On the same day, the Chamber denied the request and communicated its decision to the parties through an informal communication. The two Rule 54 bis motions are, indeed, pending before the Chamber. Their respective procedural histories are long and complex and will not be set out here, since they have already been partly described in previous decisions and will be further set out in the final decisions with regard to the two motions. The Gotovina Defence bases its request on the American Bar Association's Model Code of Judicial Conduct. It fails, however, to explain how this instrument is applicable with regard to the two Rule 54 bis motions. It does not point to any other legal basis for the remedy it is seeking. However, even assuming that the standard for the Chamber is the one set out by the Model Code and that the Chamber therefore is under an obligation to issue decisions - and I quote - "promptly," the Gotovina Defence has not explained how the Chamber has failed to do so with regard to the two Rule 54 bis motions. Neither has it argued why decisions rendered no later than 30th of April, 2010, would meet the argued standard of promptness. The Gotovina Defence's argument in this respect simply amounts to stating that the motions have been pending for a long time. However, this, in itself, does not reveal anything about how the Chamber is handling the motions. The length of time a motion is pending before a chamber obviously depends on numerous factors, including its complexity and the actions of the parties. The litigation with regard to both motions has been highly complex, and the interventions by the parties and Croatia have been numerous and lengthy. With regard to the Prosecution's Rule 54 bis motion, the Chamber has also held numerous court sessions and meetings with the parties and Croatia. In addition, with regard to both motions, the Chamber has already taken a number of necessary intermediate decisions of various kinds. In light of the foregoing reasons, the motion is denied. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. I move to the next item.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
