utterances.text: With regard to the last decision, I don't know if you want to wait till the end, but I would like to be heard on the decision that the Chamber just rendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be heard on it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would just like to ask the Chamber a question with regard to that motion. I don't know if you want me to do it at the end or if you would like me to do it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's -- are you seeking clarification or are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would just like to ask a simple question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It depends on what the question is. If it is re-opening the debate on the motion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... it's not re-opening the debate at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... okay then we'll listen to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand Your Honour has denied the motion. I'm not re-litigating that. The question for the Chamber -- I -- we -- the Gotovina Defence has for the Chamber is when we can expect a decision on that Rule 54 bis motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are working hard on it. There is a fair chance that it will not there by the 30th of April. And we tried to do it as soon afterwards. But we will spend some time first on the decision on this motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I understand, Mr. President. I mean -- and if I can just follow up the question: Are we talking 30, 60, 90 days? I mean, if we're talking about a period of time that's relatively complex, I note that the Chamber quite expeditiously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse -- may I finish, Mr. President, and put my statement on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- expeditiously gave a decision concerning the intervention by Croatia with the Gotovina Defence team, and it was, like, I think, a 36-page opinion, and the request we have at this point is can we look forward, in the very near future, to a decision on this score? And that was simply what I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, first of all, Mr. Kehoe, the Chamber is -- I don't know what -- you know about preparing decisions. That is that you have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I worked in Chambers for quite sometime, Mr. President, years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that means that we are, first of all, analysing exactly what the parties have submitted. And that is, in this case, is -- both -- in relation to both motions, quite a bit. Then you have to agree on a draft and what direction to draft the decision. Then have you to agree on those drafts. And you have to do that. Whereas, other unexpected new things often arrive. One of the things that comes to my mind is, I think, a -- well, a motion which was filed, I think today or yesterday also by the Gotovina Defence, which, of course, we have to look at as -- to see how urgent that motion is and what is exactly sought as a relief in that motion. What we do is to deliver decisions as quickly as we can under the circumstances. And if you say, Would it be 30, 60, 90, days? That's not what I expect to happen. But I can't give you any guarantees apart from that we're doing our utmost best to deliver those decisions as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I'm sure that Your Honour is aware of, as Your Honour noted, how long this has been pending and the urgency with which the parties, not just the parties in this courtroom, have put before the Court the urgency with which that decision needs to be decided. Whatever the decision happens to be, granting the Rule 54 bis motion, denying the Rule 54 bis motion, triggering rights to an immediate appeal, whatever it happens to be, it's almost in a situation where whatever the decision is, the decision is, so the parties can move on from there. But with this -- where we are right now a betwixt and between, and we ask the Court's indulgence to direct the Chamber's attention to that so we can get a decision promptly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that the Gotovina Defence developed some, perhaps, very understandable impatience is clear to the Chamber at this moment. That's what I can say about it. It is, to some extent, although not directly in relation to the 30th of April, that you're re-opening the debate on whether the 15th of May or the 30th of May would be -- I think I've said what I wanted to say about it, and you have to do it with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I then move on to my next item, and that's a clarification, Mr. Hedaraly, and I'm addressing you specifically. A clarification in relation to the Prosecution's motion to strike the Markac stipulation to sections of the Prosecution's pre-trial brief. We dealt with that in the last housekeeping session, and I then said that a certain question arises, whether it's necessary at all, and I depicted an alternative way of approaching the matter. And then you said, "That's fine with us, Mr. President." You simply wanted to point at -- now what you then said is understood by the Chamber as a withdrawal of that motion. If we have misunderstood that, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I move on to my next item. We also discussed, at the last housekeeping session, P979. We dealt with a translation issue regarding P979. There was an objection to the original translation. It was about the words "of prisoners." We had a re-translation. All parties agreed on that. I then inquired as to whether the Markac and the Cermak Defence had any objection to the revised translation which then should replace the translation which was attached to P979. I then instructed the Registrar to replace the old translation by the new one. But I think, especially because of the translation issue, P979 was not yet admitted into evidence. That was the only reason why no decision on admission had been taken yet. When I instructed the Registrar to replace the old translation by the new one, I failed to also formally -- formally admit into evidence P979. The next, and, as far as I'm concerned, the last item on a my list, is P2455. There is a translation issue there as well. The difference with the exhibit we previously discussed is that this one, despite the translation issue, that P2455 was already admitted into evidence. Now, on the 21st of April, the Prosecution has, as the Chamber understands, e-mailed the other parties to see if they consented to the -- to a revision to the translation of P2455. The Chamber would like to hear from the parties whether there's any dispute remaining or whether the revised translation is accepted by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are in the process of reviewing the document and I believe we indicated to the Prosecution that we did not believe it was appropriate at the time to e-mail Chambers as of yet before we've come to agreement, and I believe the Prosecution indicated that it was inadvertently sent to Chambers yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So we will get back to you on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll hear further from you. The only thing the Chamber is interested in is whether the matter has been resolved, yes or no, and is not interested in any dispute between the parties and what the subject matter of that dispute is. I have no further items on my agenda at this moment, but -- yes, I made the same mistake as I did yesterday. I said I failed to formally admit into evidence -- I now do admit into evidence P979. Any other matter to be raised at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just -- I think, on behalf of the Gotovina Defence, we would like, since we -- from I what understand, we'll properly adjourn sine die --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- some discussion about Scheduling Orders and how we're going to proceed in the future. I think the Chamber is aware of the Gotovina Defence's particular concerns, and we understand the re-opening is going to take place. If we can have, perhaps, a discussion again on how we wish to proceed because obviously we'd like to move things forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if we were not aware, we certainly are now, Mr. -- over the last two days, not to say that we were already aware of the urgency to proceed. Perhaps I could address Mr. Hedaraly whether he could give us -- yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think, as this directly impacts upon our rights in the trial, we will be seeking a certificate for interlocutory appeal in relation to that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The decision of re-opening?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And, therefore, in our submission, it would not be wise to start setting out a scheduling timetable with matters pertinent to that decision as well as issues that flow from it, in relation to any future Defence preparations that may need to be taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kay, the issue is whether, if the Chamber would grant a certificate for an interlocutory appeal, what, if such an appeal would be filed, what the consequences should be, whether the proceedings would have to wait until that appeal is decided upon or whether we could proceed meanwhile. Now, we have -- it's not the only matter of interlocutory appeals which will raise that question. I do agree with you that that is a matter which needs careful attention. Of course, we do not know yet what the content of your motion to seek a certificate will contain. Meanwhile, I would ask Mr. Hedaraly what he considers feasible, at all, if we would continue at this moment, what he would consider is possible. Not to say that that immediately then gets the green light of the Trial Chamber but that at least when considering these matters, that we have a full overview, legal matters, whether or not any interlocutory appeal should, at this moment, lead to further adjournments and delays. I'm not blaming anyone, but just in factual terms. And if not, in what time-frame any evidence to be presented by the Prosecution could be heard. Not to say that it will be heard in that time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In a way, the cart is going before the horse again, because we need time to prepare. And our investigations are having to take place and permissions are being sought to interview witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is not restricted just to these three witnesses. This is a far wider issue. And we have to ensure that we have everything at our disposal that is capable of dealing with such an issue. And that has to be prepared. It is a -- a new issue for us to face and deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can assure you, Mr. Kay, that everything you said until now has been the subject of discussions within the Chamber. I mean, we're not blind or so unexperienced that we are aware that certain decisions that were taken -- well, of course, will have a direct consequence that, that the course which we allowed the Prosecution to take but also that may trigger quite a lot of other matters as well, preparing for that, calling witnesses by the Defence. I mean, we have overlooked [sic] all of that. What I'm, at this moment, primarily seeking to hear from Mr. Hedaraly is what the minimum time would be for him to prepare and present the evidence he would have on his mind. Whether we would then hear that evidence within that time-frame, that's a totally different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah, as long as our position is factored into any timetable, we have no objection. But we are just very anxious to make sure that this doesn't get rushed and we are left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can ensure you that if Mr. Hedaraly said, We need five weeks, that not immediately a scheduling orders would follow that in five weeks we hear that evidence. We'll certainly, of course, ask the parties their views on the consequences of the decision, but the first one, of course, we would hear is what Mr. Hedaraly says he would need at least. And that's what I'm inquiring into at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, could you give us any indication? I think the question to you has how been phrased in some 10, 15, or 20 lines, so I hope you understand what I'm seeking.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I hope so too. And if I don't, I'm sure you will make sure to remind me. I will stay vague because we are in open session still, but the Prosecution has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could move in private session if you would prefer to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary, unless the Chamber wants more detail. But given some of the logistical issues that are involved that I believe the Chamber is familiar with, we were thinking that the week of the 17th of May would be the easier week. Any time after that, possible the week before. But because of these logistical issues, it could be tight. But that was the minimum time that we would require to -- to get the witnesses here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I take it - but I'm addressing the parties - would it be the best way to proceed by means of written decision -- by written submissions, and would you prefer to make those submissions after you have filed a request for a certificate for a interlocutory appeal, or at the same time, or after a decision has been taken on such a request for a certificate? I'm just now asking you whether written submissions - that's the first part of my question - and the second is in what time-frame you would consider to be the appropriate way of approaching the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, the drafting of the certificate, request for a certificate, is -- is taking place, and that will be filed at an early stage next week. When the Court considers that and considers the merits of it, it -- it depends what flows after that as to what direction the matter goes in. This is quite a big resource implication with it, as -- as well, because counsel and people have to become involved in dealing with this -- this matter in a -- quite a detailed way. And I'm reluctant to expend energy and resources on that at a time when they could be going -- going elsewhere. It -- it has had a knock-on consequence already in -- in our preparations. And so I would welcome that we deal with each issue on a stage-by-stage basis. The certificate, whether there is an appeal, then that matter go up to appeal to be decided, and then we see where we stand at a decision from the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you're -- at every new stage in the proceedings, we'll consider, having consulted the parties, what we need to know from the parties for any decision to be taken, whether that's a decision to further wait, or whether it's a decision to immediately proceed. But we'll do it in that way that we'll consider at every relevant stage what is best to be done, and we'll consult the parties on that. And then since we may not be in court for quite a while, it could be that either the Chamber calls for the parties to attend court or seeks written submissions on specific questions that will then be related to the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In light of the time, I will be very brief. Your Honours should know that we will also be joining in that motion to oppose the granting of the re-opening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Irrespective of how it's drafted, or -- Mr. Kay is not ready yet, but we do -- we do understand that you are seriously considering to join the motion, whether or not for additional reasons. Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Our position, again, based on the specific interests of our client in this matter is that rather than taking things -- or proverbially speaking, playing by ear, that instead of waiting to see how things develop and then in two or three weeks' time running into some of the issues that perhaps OTP will then at that point say, Now we need another two to three weeks to schedule the arrival of the witness, which would then put us into June - or "witnesses" I should say - that we already proceed with certain plans to bring witnesses. And if the need arises in the interim, we've reached an agreement on -- that we have to postpone it to a later date or something to that effect, then that assures that things are moving forward. But right now, since we don't know who's going to file which motions, what the arguments are going to be, et cetera, we just fear that we're looking at a six-to eight-week timetable to even get the witnesses here. And as you saw from our motion yesterday, obviously that's -- that would defeat the very motion that we filed yesterday, in terms of keep things on schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was perfectly clear from that motion. Of course, if the parties would -- and we always encourage -- if the parties would agree on certain matters, of course, the Chamber would be glad to hear that. Or if you would say that we would need ten days after that moment, et cetera. At the same time, I'm fully aware that the positions of the parties are such that it might be very difficult to reach any agreements other than on small, practical issues where the positions are fundamentally opposed, I would say. So, therefore, not to say that I would not further encourage you, that the Chamber is fully aware of the limits of that. Finally, before we adjourn, any other matter to be raised? Yes, if it is transcribed that we have overlooked all that, it is that we have not overlooked all that. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm reminded now to bring up an issue that came up yesterday which is that D970, the translation, was updated; and P1205 is a duplicate still with the incorrect translation. And we would ask that that exhibit be removed from evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we are now talking about the 77th -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is D970. The Trial Chamber will remember, I think, it's an artillery order from before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- the operation. P1205 was Bar tabled, I believe, with Mr. Theunens, as a duplicate of that. And that still has incorrect translations attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you would like to have --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that P1205 be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Vacated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Vacated. Another way of dealing with that, and I'm not fully at this moment acquainted with what problems could arise, to replace P1205 by a simple sheet saying "Identical to D970." That if anyone wants to look at P1205, that -- if reference is made to it in court and can't find it, that he finds the traffic sign on a page which then replaces P1205.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, is it possible that P1205 will be replaced by a reference that it is identical to D970.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and I will make sure to replace the page with a sign, as you say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't asked you about it, Mr. Hedaraly, but it seems to be a logical and simple matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: To the extent that documents are duplicates, Your Honour, that will not be a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other matter? We will adjourn sine die. But the last thing I would like to say to the parties is that the Chamber is also wanting to close this case and to deliver Judgement at the earliest possibility. There's nothing else on the mind of this Chamber as to -- not only fairly, but also in the context and within the possibilities to expeditiously, which may sound, at this moment, as a word which is not self-explanatory, but that's what the Chamber wishes to do. And, in this respect, it seems that the parties and the Chamber are on the same line. We adjourn, sine die.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned sine die.
